status: Two specific integration hypotheses retained. Neither is a demonstrated cause of the user's stain/wave. No third defensible new hypothesis was elevated.
execution: Static code/doc inspection only; no game, GPU/native launch, build, source/config/resource edits, or historical trace-payload inspection. Tests below are proposed, not executed.

evidence_documents.scope: Authenticated per-job conversion camera controls and static-byte native context variation; not batched production CB/SRV lifetime or discarded lists.
Eight isolated conversion jobs with uploaded/consumed payload authentication; no multi-evaluation production recording before submission.
Twelve native contexts vary external output initialization/binding, not production converter/composer CB rings or unsubmitted evaluations.
Authenticated native bytes/applied controls and isolated conversion/composition jobs; timing/lifetime mismatch remains distinct.
Saved-response CPU follow-up and audit of existing serialized native jobs, no new production-lifecycle test.

hypotheses.title: Mapped constants and shader-visible descriptors can be rewritten before earlier recorded dispatches consume them
hypotheses.confidence: High confidence in source lifetime hazard and replay mismatch; actual game trigger and stain causation unknown.
hypotheses.trigger: Fourth FloorSeed/conversion call on one feature while the first call has not consumed its slot; can be made unambiguous by recording four production-equivalent evaluations before any ExecuteCommandLists. Actual game CPU frame latency by itself is not proof: an external caller might guarantee retirement before reuse.

source_refs.meaning: Upload buffer allocated once, persistently mapped, slot memcpy and modulo advance each Dispatch, same heap rewritten and recorded CB GPU address/table handles; Unmap only in destruction. No completion check in ring reuse.
FloorSeed=3 slots; conversion=3; FloorFilter=18 at 5 calls/evaluation; composition=9 shared by composition and Blit.
Each slot owns shader-visible heap; CreateSRV/UAV overwrites its actual heap positions.
D3D12 descriptor writes target reused heap CPU handles; table binding does not copy per-dispatch immutable descriptors.
Outer production NGX caller records feature evaluation on provided command list; no slot retirement guard/queue execution or wait on this path.
Feature and postprocess commands recorded without a completion guard.
Local input-probe code explicitly notes the title queue is unseen; its generation token does not gate ComputeState ring reuse.
Queue hook associates and signals trace tickets; it does not wait before ComputeState updates.
Ticket fence tracking is separate from ring slots; no ComputeState Arm registration exists.
Standalone native runner resets/uploads/dispatches each frame, executes and waits before next frame reuse.
Standalone shader runner similarly completes GPU work before returning/reuse.

hypotheses.impact: Earlier dispatch may read later frame's jitter, matrix, origins, flags, or source resource views. This invalidates the comparison between intended frozen CPU bytes and actual production-consumed inputs; wrong temporal correspondence or changing radiance split can appear as spatial stains/waves.
minimal_test: Use four small frozen/synthetic frames with distinct per-frame CB fingerprints and immutable per-frame title texture resources. Record 4 production-equivalent FloorSeed/filter/conversion evaluations before first Execute/Signal; preserve stage outputs after each evaluation with GPU copies to dedicated snapshots.

Capture consumed CB fingerprints/input resource identities on GPU, not only CPU job payloads. Compare original rings against same command order with one immutable CB allocation and shader-visible descriptor heap per dispatch.

Also test 3 evaluations (pre-wrap negative control). FloorFilter wrap occurs during 4th full evaluation (20 calls >18); test composition with 10 calls (9 slots) and shared composition/Blit call counts independently. Do conversion/composition-only stages first to isolate wrapper lifetime from native variability.

Only after byte-level stage mismatch is isolated, use matched native replay outputs to measure whether eliminating overwrite removes wave/stain metrics. All tests are proposals and require separate authorization to execute GPU work.
hypotheses.falsification: Within the tested recording envelope, consumed CB fingerprints/resource identities and all intermediate output bits equal immutable-storage arm despite forced wrap, or source/caller proof establishes the first slot is GPU-retired before every reuse. Equal final RGB alone is insufficient with constant CB/resources. Even a positive isolated overwrite does not prove the game ever triggers it.

hypotheses.title: Discarded successful recordings advance CPU native and composition history without submitted GPU history
hypotheses.confidence: High confidence in source bookkeeping mismatch conditional on list discard; occurrence in game and color effect unverified.
hypotheses.trigger: Caller records a successful evaluation then Reset/discards its command list without Execute, or drops a partially recorded evaluation after a later stage fails. Next evaluation lacks an explicit Reset. Normal in-order eventual submission is safe for this hypothesis and does not require CPU waiting for GPU completion.

source_refs.meaning: CPU previous camera/jitter and has-history commit after API recording succeeds, before submission; successful Evaluate marks composition history commit. A failed later upscale returns false without clearing the already committed native-history flag.
CPU ping-pong history read index advances on successful normal Evaluate, not actual submission. Dropping that list selects an older GPU metadata/decision buffer as though newly written.
Explicit history invalidation exists, but command-list reset/discard is not wired to it.
Reset hook calls trace-ticket discard tracking only, not feature history invalidation.
ResetSucceeded acts on registered trace tickets only.
All replay frames are submitted/waited; no discarded successful frame exercises the production bookkeeping path.

hypotheses.impact: Next motion/jitter/previous-camera controls can describe the discarded recording rather than the last submitted frame; native RESET remains false and helper history index references an older GPU write. A dropped frame with different camera/source/jitter can therefore reuse incompatible history.
minimal_test: Warm two submitted synthetic/frozen frames, record a third with a distinct source/jitter token, then legally Reset its unsubmitted command list. Record and submit the next frame with no user Reset.

Keep immutable CB/descriptors and fence after each actually submitted frame, so H1 cannot confound this test. Compare dropped-list original bookkeeping against a matched arm that invalidates native/helper histories and rebuilds previous controls from the last submitted frame.
Authenticate emitted RESET flags, current/previous jitter, camera delta, helper-history read index/generation and actual stage RGB. Also run in-order submitted control with identical recording calls.

Start with CPU state-transition instrumentation (no GPU required) proving the dropped evaluation changes those controls. A later GPU replay is needed to establish actual radiance/history impact; not executed in this review.
hypotheses.falsification: A submission-aware path demonstrably rolls back/invalidates feature native and composition history after unsubmitted Reset, or captured next-frame controls/read generation and RGB equal last-submitted-history reference for nontrivial dropped frames. Caller proof that all successful/partially recorded RR evaluations are eventually submitted in order excludes this trigger in that caller.

not_claimed: No current-alpha game capture or game-quality fix.
No SDK defect or native internal race claim.
No new normal/camera/output-alpha sweep or estimator cosmetic recommendation.
A caller-side queue completion policy may prevent H1; lack of a guard in inspected OptiScaler source does not prove absent external synchronization.
